title: F013 leftovers — the last code that does not follow THE SYNTAX
summary: Seven cleanups found in the 2026-11-24 review: children by position, hand positions, child-in-constructor wrappers, chrome side signals, literal numbers, the terminal's own size write, stale docs.
description:
Created 2026-11-24 with Antonio's approval, from a review of F013's accepted decisions against main (c2768ec4). F013 had no phases; this phase holds what is still open. Estimate given to Antonio: 13–20 agent hours plus about 4 eye checks.

## Already done (not in this phase)
Declarative child lists (T569); Input placeholder/value following a value; described events beyond press/change/toggle; command palette and Dialog composed (P087(F011)/T469); live width/height/max sizes (`LiveValue`, `IntoLengthValue`, `Base.size_values`).

## Left out on purpose
Moving docks from the `Provider` trait (heca/src/providers/mod.rs:61) to components, and get / at_index on the regions queue (heca/src/chrome/docks/regions.rs, thread_local) — Antonio, 2026-11-24: "il 7 lo lasciamo com'è".

## Tasks
1. Children taken by position → named / declared children.
2. Positions written by hand (shift_subtree in widgets, at_rect and bounds writes in the app) → layout does it.
3. Wrappers that take their child in the constructor → `.child(..)`.
4. `ChromeSignals` / `chrome_signature` side signals → events and live values.
5. Literal numbers: glow values, BAR_W / CHECK_SIZE / RAIL_ICON_SIZE, `Icon::size(px)` → theme tokens / shares.
6. The terminal component writes its own 100% width/height.
7. AGENTS.md and docs/widget-architecture.md teach the imperative state write.

## Rules for every task
THE SYNTAX (CLAUDE.md). Cleanup never changes the look: any visible change is a proposal to Antonio first. Fixes go in the library where no caller has to know. Every new test is checked by sabotage. Visual work needs Antonio's eye check before commit. Update docs/widgets.md and in-file comments for every widget touched.

tasks.description:

Widgets: tree_layout.rs (6), tile.rs (4), input/content.rs (4), input/component.rs (4), resizable/mod.rs (3), message_list.rs (2), flex/mod.rs (2), flex/clip.rs (1), tag.rs (1) — all under heca-grid-ui/src/widgets/.

Fix: a widget that needs one of its parts holds it by name (a field or a keyed child the widget itself declared), or the part reads a live value instead of being reached into. When the same need shows up in several widgets, the library gets the builder once (Rule Zero), not a copy per widget.

tasks.title: No widget or composition writes a position by hand — layout places everything
tasks.description:
THE SYNTAX: never write a bound or a position by hand. Found on main 2026-11-24:

- `shift_subtree` (moving children after layout) used by widgets: heca-grid-ui/src/widgets/tooltip.rs, toast/stack.rs, scroll_region/mod.rs + motion.rs, select/component.rs, overlay/mod.rs, context_menu/presenter.rs, flex/mod.rs. Its definition and the paint transform (lib.rs, component/tree.rs, component/paint_cx/transform.rs) are the framework side; scrolling offsets may legitimately stay a paint transform — decide per case and say why.
- Bounds written by hand in the app: heca/src/providers/workspaces/column_group.rs:138, heca/src/chrome/panes/column/mod.rs:122.
- `.at_rect(..)` in the app: chrome/panes/terminal/links.rs, terminal/viewport.rs, terminal/search/mod.rs, chrome/panes/column/shell.rs, chrome/surfaces/expose/workspace_row.rs.

Fix: placement is said as layout (Overlay position / anchor, grid tracks, flex, offsets as live values), so the framework computes it. A floating surface uses the overlay's placement; scrolling uses the scroll region's own offset.

Risk: these are overlay / tooltip / toast / select / scroll — visual work; nothing ships without Antonio driving it in the GPU app.

tasks.title: The chrome's side signals (ChromeSignals, chrome_signature) are replaced by events and live values
tasks.description:
THE EVENTS: a state change is heard with `cx.on("name", ..)`, never a dedicated signal bundle. `ChromeSignals` (heca/src/chrome/window/signals.rs:26) and `chrome_signature` (heca/src/chrome/window/retained.rs:38, a hash deciding when the chrome rebuilds) are still used — 34 uses in: lib.rs, app/frame/panes.rs, providers/mod.rs, providers/workspaces/pane_row.rs + seams.rs, chrome/mod.rs, chrome/input/dispatch.rs, chrome/state/workspaces.rs, chrome/window/{theme, retained, scene/mod, signals}.rs, chrome/docks/contribution.rs, handlers/docks/mod.rs.

Fix: each value a widget shows is a live value it reads (it updates itself), and each change a component reacts to is an event raised from one place (contract: P054(F006) "Pane runtime state", section 0.1). The rebuild-by-signature goes away where a live value or keyed children make the rebuild unnecessary; what still needs a rebuild says so through the same event. Do not touch the dock `Provider` API (left out, see the phase).

Check: tests; sidebar, pane rows and bars update exactly as today (Antonio eye check: rename, cwd change, agent status, workspace switch).

tasks.description:

tasks.title: A flex child never shrinks below its content — the automatic minimum, as CSS min-height:auto
tasks.description:
Reported by heca-pro-dev 2026-11-24 while testing heca-pro's rooms dock; Antonio approved, to do next with F013's work.

## The defect
A child can end up smaller than its content, so text overlaps with no warning.
Case: a Row holding a Flex::column with two children — a Grid (name line) with `.flex(1.0)` and a report line under it. The grid starts from height 0, gets less than its content, and the report line is drawn over the name. Measured: name at y=3 h=19, report at y=12. heca-pro worked around it (no `flex` on that grid; test heca-pro-components/src/member/tests.rs `the_report_line_sits_below_the_name`); the trap stays open for everyone else.

## Cause (verified 2026-11-24)
heca-grid-ui/src/layout/build.rs:125-129: for a flex child with `parts > 0`, layout sets `flex_basis = 0`, **`min_height = min_height.or(Some(Px(0.0)))`** and `flex_shrink = 1`. The forced `min_height = 0` removes the content minimum. CSS gives a flex item `min-height: auto` (main axis), so it never shrinks below its content's minimum size.

## Fix
In the layout, once: a flex child's minimum along the main axis is its content's minimum unless the author set one explicitly (`.min_height(..)` / `.min_width(..)`, including 0). No component author has to know the trap. Check the other axis/direction (a row's main axis is width), Grid children (skipped today, `in_a_grid`), and every place that relied on the 0 minimum to let a share shrink (docks, sidebars, pane columns, ScrollRegion content) — those must say `min_height(0)` explicitly or keep working through their own overflow.

## Check
A test with the reported shape (name grid with `.flex(1.0)` above a report line) asserting the report line starts below the name; a test that an explicit `min_height(0)` still lets a share shrink; sabotage both. Whole heca-grid-ui + heca suites; Antonio's eye check over sidebar docks, panes and dialogs (layout is visual).

---
**Completion summary:**
Shipped in PR #363 (branch feat/t587-flex-content-minimum), two commits; CI green on Windows, macOS, Linux.

7ee25ceb — T587. Decided with Antonio 2026-11-24 after measuring: CSS's automatic minimum applied where it does not break docks. `.flex(n)` no longer forces min_height 0 (heca-grid-ui/src/layout/build.rs), and a grid's UNWRITTEN tracks are `fr(1)` (minimum = content, heca-grid-ui/src/style/layout.rs to_taffy_grid). A WRITTEN `1fr` stays `minmax(0, 1fr)` (style/grid.rs Track::Fr): applying CSS there too made the first of two docks take 956px of 900 even with a scrolling body (dock_body test) — CSS does the same, sidebars in CSS use minmax(0,1fr). The real cause of heca-pro's overlap was both: the one-column grid's implicit row had minimum 0 AND `.flex` forced min_height 0. docs/layout.md table updated.

5a7f3023 — found during the eye check, Antonio asked to fix at once in this branch: (1) dock resize fell behind the pointer — handlers/docks/mod.rs handle_resize_container read heights from the screen each step while several steps run before a layout; now starts from the hand shares the last step wrote (ChromeHost::hand_share added, current_heights/heights_from_shares/resized_shares pure fns, handlers/docks/resize_tests.rs). (2) a lone open dock (neighbour folded) filled only its share fraction — build.rs scales flex parts that sum below 1 to sum 1.

Verification: new tests sabotaged (fr_share: a_child_that_does_not_scroll_never_gets_less_than_its_content, a_scrolling_child_keeps_its_parts_however_much_it_holds, an_explicit_zero_minimum_still_lets_a_child_shrink, parts_that_add_up_to_less_than_one_still_share_all_the_room; resize_tests x3); a_grid_with_no_template test changed to content that fits (old one encoded minimum 0). Layout timing measured: <1 ms per pass on main and branch alike. heca-grid-ui + heca + heca-view-realize green; clippy macOS + Windows clean. Antonio's eye check: docks, panes, dialogs, palette as before; resize follows the pointer; lone dock fills.

Known: with the glow theme a dock shows two borders (seen during T580's check), not investigated.

tasks.title: Sidebar pane views — compact / normal / extended lists, a current-pane list, switched by an action and remembered
tasks.description:
Asked by Antonio 2026-11-24 (shape and names his; screenshot: extended = title + cwd + git + agent, normal = title + cwd + git, compact = title + cwd).

## Config — [appearance.sidebar]
```toml
pane_view          = "extended"                          # the view heca starts in: compact | normal | extended
pane_compact_view  = ["cwd", "agent"]
pane_normal_view   = ["git", "cwd", "agent"]
pane_extended_view = ["title", "git", "cwd", "agent"]
pane_current_view  = ["title", "git", "cwd", "agent"]    # the current pane's lines; unset = follows the active view
```
- Each view is a list of line names, in the order written. Names: "title", "cwd", "git", "agent", and lines added by programs built on heca (e.g. "demo.status").
- **"title" becomes a line** like the others: the pane's name with its icon. The status dot (green pip) follows the title line; in a view without "title" it goes on the first line (Antonio: "prima riga se fattibile").
- Replaces today's `pane_lines` (heca-config/src/appearance/sidebar.rs:36, config.default.toml:750): retired with the usual notice for keys heca no longer reads (heca-config/src/loader/unread.rs).

## Switching
- An action, through the ActionRegistry, keybinding registry and RPC as always: set a view by name (argument) AND cycle to the next one. In the command palette with a label.
- The change is an event (`sidebar.pane_view.changed`, THE EVENTS) so plugins and the scripts' stream hear it.

## Remembered
- The chosen view is saved with `heca_config::state_file` (data folder, JSON, versioned, atomic; same helper as search-history.json / announced.json, and T528 for dock placement). At start the saved view wins, else `pane_view`. A config reload whose `pane_view` changed resets to it (as a sidebar's visibility, T532). Confirm this precedence with Antonio before building.

## How (current state, verified 2026-11-24)
heca/src/providers/workspaces/pane_row.rs:146-186 builds the row as a `Tile` (status, icon, title, suffix) and appends one line per `ws_state.pane_lines()` entry; every line is a `Visibility` that decides for itself, and the row knows if it is `active`. So a view is: which named lines are visible, read live from one signal (active view + current-pane list), no sidebar rebuild. The title moving into the line list means Tile's title/status slots become driven by the list (the dot on the title line, else the first line).

## Check
Tests (sabotaged): each view shows its lines in order; the current pane uses pane_current_view, unset follows; no title → dot on first line; action set/cycle + event; saved view restored, config reload resets. docs/configuration.md + config.default.toml. Clippy macOS + Windows, CI. Antonio's eye check of the three views and the current pane.
